summary: Guidance requested: traffic-gated demotion plan for hybrid batching + KV-prefetch + quant experiment
description: Customer Novalune ran an experiment that enabled KV-prefetch + aggressive batching and switched a subset of traffic to a q4 quantization profile on their Dedicated pool. After the change they report intermittent 5xx errors (mostly 503/504) and sporadic tail-latency spikes on a small set of high-concurrency routes. Customer is asking for a stepwise, low-risk demotion/rollback plan that preserves throughput for unaffected routes and avoids mass disruption.
impact: Several production routes for Novalune see increased 5xxs and 95/99p latency jumps affecting downstream user-facing features for ~5% of traffic. No full-region outage. Billing not impacted yet. Customer requests resolution window within their dedicated SLA window.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer enabled mixed-precision q4 variant for model redwood-llama-13b on Dedicated pool 'nl-prod-1'
2) Enabled kv-prefetch = true and batch_target_tokens = 2048 (aggressive) at tenant-level optimizer profile
3) Routed 20% of production traffic for two routes (/chat/v1 and /summaries) to the new profile via traffic-split
4) Within 30-90 minutes, monitoring shows increased 503/504 and per-request token latency tail growth on those routes

investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: aggressive batching combined with KV-prefetch increases memory pressure and scheduling contention on dense GPU nodes, causing throttled worker launches and intermittent gateway 503s. Alternate hypothesis: q4 quant path increases kernel contention for longer contexts leading to scheduler backpressure. Correlated events: autoscaler logs show several transient pod restarts and NVIDIA MIG fragment reclamation around 15:10-15:20 UTC. Grafana dashboards: serving/runtime->per-node-queue-length and scheduler->allocation-latency show spikes coincident with errors. No IP/TLS or DNS abnormalities observed.
temporary_mitigations_applied: 1) Rolled traffic split back from 20% -> 5% for affected routes as immediate mitigation. 2) Enabled internal per-tenant circuit threshold (route-level reject at 2% 5xx) to prevent broader impact. 3) Increased autoscaler buffer for Dedicated pool by +1 GPU for 30 minutes to relieve pressure. These reduced error rate to baseline for most routes but some tail latency remained.
recommended_safe_demote_procedure:
We recommend a conservative, traffic-gated demotion rather than a blunt revert to avoid cache churn. Steps: 
- Create a snapshot of current optimizer profile (API: /admin/optimizer/snapshot) before changes. 
- Open a controlled canary window: shift traffic for affected routes to a 'stable' profile incrementally: 10% -> 0% in 5-minute steps (reduce 10 percentage points every 5 minutes). 
- After each step, monitor: per-route 95p/99p latency, 5xx rate, per-node queue length, and scheduler allocation-latency for 2x median request window. 
- If 5xx doesn't fall or allocation-latency remains high after a step, pause and add +1 GPU to pool (temporary warm capacity) and wait 10 minutes. 
- When traffic reaches 0% on experimental profile: evict KV-prefetch caches for affected tenant routes using lightweight eviction API (do not full-evict global caches) to avoid cold-start storm. 
- Switch model variant from q4 -> q8 for the tenant routes in a single atomic config change, but keep batch targets conservative (batch_target_tokens=512). 
- Observe for a 30-minute warmup before reintroducing traffic. 
- If problems persist, restore snapshot (rollback) and open an internal incident for runtime-level investigation.
Notes: prefer traffic-split adjustments over global toggles; avoid full cluster-wide cache clears; use per-route gating to isolate impact.
postmortem_and_followup_actions: 1) Create route-level automated 'demote' runbook entry in Confluence and link it to Console's optimizer UI. 2) Add an autoscale buffer guard for tenant-level optimizer experiments to pre-warm capacity for +5% traffic changes. 3) Add a short-circuit circuit-breaker in the serving-runtime for kv-prefetch melt-down patterns (queue-length > 300). 4) Schedule an engineering pairing session with Novalune for a staged re-run in staging with synthetic traffic to validate warmup parameters.
resolution: Work in progress: Applied incremental traffic rollback to 0% for experimental profile and performed kv-prefetch per-tenant eviction; switched tenant routes to q8 with conservative batching. Error rates returned to baseline on primary routes. Customer accepted the staged demote plan and requested a follow-up runbook with explicit API calls and thresholds. No code changes required; configuration-only changes.
